conclusion: We introduce a fixed-support route-transport framework in which histories can be equivalent at a current event interface yet differ as predictors of later admissible observations. For each interface, we define a current quotient by present-event indistinguishability and a predictive quotient by equality of all later admissible event statistics under continuation. Standard quotient-algebraic results then apply in this setting: future-predictive equivalence refines current-event equivalence, admissible continuations induce well-defined transport on , and the current class after transport is determined by the source predictive class through a canonical mixed map _i _j . Generic transport on along all outgoing continuations exists precisely at flat interfaces, where current equivalence already determines all future observations. The predictive quotient is future-sufficient, and every future-sufficient state abstraction factors uniquely through on the reachable image. Strict refinement of is equivalent to existence of a pair of histories that are current-equivalent but future-distinct. For endo-continuations, representative push can preserve the current class of every history while moving a predictive class. The contribution of the paper is the framework itself and the demonstration that it is non-vacuous: an axiom-audited finite memory-wheel instance in Lean and exact finite fixed-support benchmarks instantiate strict refinement and the loop asymmetry, while the computational suite separates artifact, flattenable, explicit-latent, dissipative, and coherent-candidate regimes with bounded robustness under perturbation. Small discovery searches recover additional coherent candidates beyond the hand-built examples while a control search space remains all-flat.

source_wording_tex: We introduce a fixed-support route-transport framework in which histories can be equivalent at a current event interface yet differ as predictors of later admissible observations. For each interface, we define a current quotient $\CurrentQ$ by present-event indistinguishability and a predictive quotient $\PredictiveQ$ by equality of all later admissible event statistics under continuation. Standard quotient-algebraic results then apply in this setting: future-predictive equivalence refines current-event equivalence, admissible continuations induce well-defined transport on $\PredictiveQ$, and the current class after transport is determined by the source predictive class through a canonical mixed map $\PredictiveQ_i\to\CurrentQ_j$. The predictive quotient is future-sufficient, and every future-sufficient state abstraction factors uniquely through $\PredictiveQ$ on the reachable image. Strict refinement of $\PredictiveQ \to \CurrentQ$ is equivalent to existence of a pair of histories that are current-equivalent but future-distinct. For endo-continuations, representative push can preserve the current class of every history while moving a predictive class. The contribution of the paper is the framework itself and the demonstration that it is non-vacuous: an axiom-audited finite memory-wheel instance in Lean and exact finite fixed-support benchmarks instantiate strict refinement and the loop asymmetry, while the computational suite separates artifact, flattenable, explicit-latent, dissipative, and coherent-candidate regimes with bounded robustness under perturbation. Section~\ref{sec:route-transport-packages} defines route transport packages, the two equivalence relations, the current and predictive quotients, and the comparison map. expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{thm:predictive-transport}
For every admissible continuation $\gamma\in\mathcal{C}_{i\to j}$, pushing representatives along $\gamma$ descends to a well-defined predictive transport
\[
T^{M}_{\gamma} : \PredictiveQ_i \to \PredictiveQ_j.
\]
It also descends to a mixed map
\[
\widehat T^{M\toQ}_{\gamma} :
\PredictiveQ_i \to \CurrentQ_j,
\qquad
[h]_{\FutureEquiv_i}\longmapsto
[\operatorname{push}_{\gamma}h]_{\CurrentEquiv_j},
\]
and these maps form the commutation triangle
\[
\pi_j \circ T^{M}_{\gamma}
=
\widehat T^{M\toQ}_{\gamma}.
\]
For a fixed source interface $i$, current-event equivalence is stable under every outgoing push if and only if $i$ is flat:
\[
\bigl(h\CurrentEquiv_i h'\Longrightarrow h\FutureEquiv_i h'\bigr)
\quad\text{for all }h,h'\in\Histories_i.
\]
Thus current-quotient transport induced by representative push along every outgoing continuation is available exactly in the flat case, not as part of an arbitrary route transport package.

\label{thm:reachable-factorization}
Let $s : \Histories_i \to S$ be any future-sufficient state abstraction at interface $i$. Then on the reachable image
\[
\operatorname{Reach}(s) := \{\,s(h) : h\in\Histories_i\,\},
\]
there exists a factor map
\[
f : \operatorname{Reach}(s) \to \PredictiveQ_i
\]
such that
\[
f(s(h)) = [h]_{\FutureEquiv_i}
\qquad

\label{thm:reachable-factorization}
Let $s : \Histories_i \to S$ be any future-sufficient state abstraction at interface $i$. Then on the reachable image
\[
\operatorname{Reach}(s) := \{\,s(h) : h\in\Histories_i\,\},
\]
there exists a factor map
\[
f : \operatorname{Reach}(s) \to \PredictiveQ_i
\]
such that
\[
f(s(h)) = [h]_{\FutureEquiv_i}
\qquad
\text{for all } h\in\Histories_i.
\]
Moreover, this factorization is unique on the reachable image: if two maps from $\operatorname{Reach}(s)$ to $\PredictiveQ_i$ agree with the predictive quotient on all histories, then they agree everywhere on $\operatorname{Reach}(s)$.

Let $\ell\in\mathcal{C}_{i\to i}$ be a loop at interface $i$. Then $\ell$ induces the predictive endomorphism
\[
L^{M}_{\ell} : \PredictiveQ_i \to \PredictiveQ_i.

\[
\operatorname{push}_{\ell}h \CurrentEquiv_i h
\qquad\text{for every }h\in\Histories_i,

\[
L^{M}_{\ell}(q)\neq q

\]

conclusion: Beyond the scope boundaries stated in Section , two further limitations deserve mention. The Lean formalization is intentionally partial: it covers the quotient comparison, predictive and mixed transport, the flatness characterization, sufficiency on the reachable image, witness/strict-refinement equivalence, representative-level loop asymmetry, and a finite non-vacuity instance, but does not yet formalize moved-class sets, cardinality-based nontriviality criteria, or richer action-level invariants. Those omissions do not undermine the present results, but they mark the current boundary of the formal development. The benchmark and discovery labels should also be read operationally rather than ontologically. In particular, coherent_candidate denotes a benchmark or discovered candidate that exhibits the loop asymmetry and witness structure targeted by the paper. It is not a claim that a stronger external state representation has been forced.

expanded_source_wording_tex: At the level of adjacent literatures, the predictive quotient is closest to future-oriented state constructions such as causal states, observable operator models, and predictive state representations \citep{ShaliziCrutchfield2001ComputationalMechanics,Jaeger2000ObservableOperatorModels,LittmanSuttonSingh2002PredictiveRepresentationsState}. The current/future comparison layer added here is closer in spirit to a comparison between observational and behavioral equivalence, and thus also sits near bisimulation traditions in concurrency and probabilistic processes \citep{Park1981ConcurrencyAutomata,Milner1989CommunicationConcurrency,LarsenSkou1991BisimulationThroughProbabilisticTesting}. The paper does not claim to subsume those frameworks. Its claim is narrower: on fixed support, one can compare what is visible now with what matters later, and one can separate flat, artifactual, removable, currentizable, dissipative, and loop-asymmetric cases within one operational language.

conclusion: The abstract route-transport package consists of a fixed support object, a family of interfaces, interface-indexed history sets, typed continuation sets, interface-indexed event sets, and the operations of identity continuation, continuation composition, representative push, and current observation, subject to identity and composition laws for push. The two fundamental equivalence relations are current-event equivalence and future-predictive equivalence. Their quotients define the current quotient Q and the predictive quotient M , with canonical comparison map pi : M → Q induced by refinement. The finite implementation of Section should be read as an exact model of this abstract package rather than as a separate semantics. In particular, the benchmark and discovery sections do not change the theorem layer; they instantiate it.

\subsection{Current formal scope}\label{appsubsec:lean-scope}
The Lean development currently covers the quotient comparison story needed for the paper: equivalence refinement, predictive transport, the mixed predictive-to-current triangle, the flatness characterization for current push stability, reachable-image sufficiency and factorization, witness strictness, representative-level loop asymmetry, and finite non-vacuity. It does not yet formalize moved-class sets, cardinality-based nontriviality criteria, or richer action-level invariants. Those omissions are real, but they do not undercut any theorem claim made in the main body.
